name: BIT 4484 Notes 8 9 2020
excerpt: BIT 4484 Notes 8 9 2020 covers monitoring and controlling in project management.
notes:
- Monitoring and controlling is a key aspect of project management.
- Expert judgement involves using one's own intuition.
- Earned Value Management measures project performance based on scope, schedule, and cost.
- Planned Value (PV) is the portion of the approved total cost estimate planned to be spent during a given period.
- Actual Costs (AC) are the total costs actually incurred.
- Rate of Performance (RP) is the amount of work completed as a proportion of work expected to be completed at a given time.
- Earned Value (EV) is the estimate of the value of work performed in a given period.
- Cost Variance (CV) compares budgeted cost vs actual costs.
- Schedule Variance (SV) compares work performed vs actual work performed.
- SV is calculated as EV minus PV.
- Cost Performance Index (CPI) measures the financial effectiveness of a project, with CPI = EV / AC, and a value greater than 1 is good.
- Schedule Performance Index (SPI) measures how close the project is to schedule, with SPI = EV / PV, and a value greater than 1 is good.
- Estimate at Completion is the best guess for how much money will be spent at the end of the project.
- Scope Creep is the tendency of scope to increase over time.
- The Wasa was a warship.
- Changes to the Wasa included speeding up the ship, increasing its length to 120 feet, then changing it to 111 feet, needing double cannons, and requiring much more space.
- The Wasa ship sunk after 15 minutes.
- Project Schedule Management involves knowing the status of the schedule, influencing factors that can cause schedule issues, determining whether the schedule has changed, and managing changes when they occur.
- A slipped milestone is a milestone reached later than expected.
- Sponsors hate surprises the most.
- Being clear and honest with sponsors is important.
- Control Charts illustrate results of a process over time.
- The Seven Run Rule examines if there is a problem if there are 7 data points in a row above or below the mean.
- A Pareto Chart is a bar chart with a cumulative percentage as a line.
- The 80%/20% rule states that 80% of problems come from 20% of causes.
- Stratification involves separating data to see patterns.
- Workarounds are unplanned responses to risk events.
- Constructive Change Orders are oral or written requests made by someone with authority.

Closing Projects - Chapter 9 

Closing

Closing Methods

Integration - Project completed successfully, integrated into operations

Most common

Addition - New unit added to company as result of project

Extinction - Project done, no addition or integration

Extinction by murder - Higher up kills project

Starvation - Project ends by stopping funding

Withdrawal of life support

Outputs

Transition plan - Final product, processes, and instructions to use them

Lessons Learned Report - Major takeaways for a future project

Close-out Meeting

Opposite of a kickoff meeting

Includes major stakeholders

Knowledge Transfer - Sharing of knowledge gained during project

Employee knowledge, human capital, is the key asset of company

Challenger

Failure with O-Ring

People at lower levels could not communicate with top levels
